A first stop before [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd). Short sections, one idea each. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the PPG Wave is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **PPG Wave** was "built by the German company Palm Products GmbH from 1981 to 1987" (Wikipedia, "PPG Wave").
- Wolfgang Palm pioneered **wavetable synthesis**, the idea behind it (Wikipedia).
- The Wave 2.3 has eight voices (PPG *Wave 2.3 Service Manual*, p. 5).

## Its sound

- A **wavetable** is a row of 64 different waves; the Wave 2.3 has 30 of them (Sound On Sound, "PPG Wave 2.3 & Waveterm B").
- An envelope or LFO can **move through the table**, so the tone changes while a note plays.
- After the digital waves comes an **analog filter**, the SSM 2044, 24 dB per octave (service manual, p. 5; Wikipedia).
- The four tables on this page are the page's own, not the PPG's real ones.

This is the PPG Wave panel from [Classic Synths Compared](synth-compare.qmd), drawn after the real one (not a copy). ## Guided tour

Each step loads a worked example and changes one thing. Learn more in [Sound 9: Wavetable](sound-wavetable.qmd).

```{=html}
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ppg-sweep" data-set="{&quot;envWave&quot;:0}"><p><b>One wave, standing still.</b> Envelope 1 does not move the wave. Listen: a steady tone.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ppg-sweep"><p><b>The envelope moves the wave.</b> <b>Env 1 → wave</b> at 50. Listen: each note changes colour as it plays.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ppg-sweep" data-set="{&quot;waveA&quot;:40,&quot;waveB&quot;:40,&quot;envWave&quot;:0}"><p><b>A different wave.</b> Start further along the table. Listen: a new tone.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ppg-pad" data-set="{&quot;lfoWave&quot;:0}"><p><b>A pad, no LFO.</b> Listen: smooth and still.</p></div>
<div class="ik-step" data-ex="ppg-pad"><p><b>The LFO moves the wave.</b> <b>LFO → wave</b> at 20. Listen for a slow, glassy shimmer.</p></div>
```

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "PPG Wave":

- used by a-ha, Alphaville, Bronski Beat and David Bowie

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>A wavetable is…</b></p><ul><li>A row of different waves</li><li>A table for a drum kit</li><li>A mixing desk</li><li>A guitar effect</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Sound On Sound.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What makes the tone move during a note?</b></p><ul><li>An envelope or LFO moving through the table</li><li>Turning the volume</li><li>Changing the tempo</li><li>Nothing</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Steps 2 and 5.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Which country was PPG from?</b></p><ul><li>Germany</li><li>Japan</li><li>USA</li><li>Brazil</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Wikipedia.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>Is the PPG&#x27;s filter digital or analog?</b></p><ul><li>Analog (SSM 2044)</li><li>Digital</li><li>It has no filter</li><li>Made of water</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Service manual p. 5.</p></div>
```

Eight voices, digital oscillators with wavetable EPROMs, SSM 2044 filters, panel pots reading 0-63 (PDF p. 5). No owner's manual was found. A scan, read by OCR.

"PPG Wave." *Wikipedia*, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PPG_Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PPG_Wave). Years of the Wave 2, 2.2 and 2.3; two oscillators a voice on the 2.2 and 2.3; SSM 2044 24 dB filters.

Sound On Sound. "PPG Wave 2.3 & Waveterm B" [review]. *Sound On Sound*, [www.soundonsound.com/reviews/ppg-wave-23-waveterm-b](https://www.soundonsound.com/reviews/ppg-wave-23-waveterm-b). 64 waves make a wavetable; 30 wavetables on the Wave 2.3.
:::
